---
title: Get started
description: Install smalldocs, make a site, preview it and publish it.
order: 1
---

## Install smalldocs

smalldocs needs Python 3.11 or later. Add it to a project as a development tool:

```bash
uv add --dev smalldocs     # or: pip install smalldocs
```

If the site documents the API of your package, install smalldocs in the environment of the package.
smalldocs imports the package to read its code.

## Make a site

A project is a folder with a `_smalldocs.yml` file and some pages. A page is a Markdown file, `.md` or
`.qmd`, or a Jupyter notebook, `.ipynb`. A `.qmd` file is Markdown with some additions, such as callouts
and tabs. [Writing pages](markdown.qmd) describes them. Front matter is the YAML block between two `---`
lines at the top of a page. It holds the options of the page, such as its title.

The smallest site has three files:

::: {.panel-tabset}
## _smalldocs.yml

```yaml
project:
  type: website

website:
  title: "My project"
  navbar:
    left:
      - href: index.qmd
        text: Home
      - about.qmd

theme: cosmo
toc: true
```

## index.qmd

```markdown
---
title: My project
---

My project does one thing well. Read [about it](about.qmd).
```

## about.qmd

```markdown
---
title: About
---

## Who made it

We did.
```
:::

## Build the site

```bash
smalldocs render            # the folder you are in
smalldocs render docs       # or another folder
```

smalldocs writes the site into the output folder. The output folder is `_site`, or the folder that the
option `project.output-dir` names. Each build deletes the old content of the output folder first. Open
`_site/index.html` in a browser, or serve the folder.

## Preview the site

```bash
smalldocs preview docs
```

The command builds the site, serves it at `http://127.0.0.1:4200` and opens your browser. When you save
a file, smalldocs builds the site again, and the browser loads the new pages. To use another port, give
`--port`.

::: {.callout-tip}
## Generated pages do not start a loop

A `pre-render` script, or the API reference, writes pages during a build. After each build, `preview`
notes the time of each file again. So the pages that a build writes do not start another build.
:::

## Publish the site

To put the site on GitHub Pages, run:

```bash
smalldocs publish gh-pages docs
```

The command builds the site and commits it to the branch `gh-pages`. It works in a temporary copy of
the repository, called a worktree, and then pushes the branch to `origin`. Your files and your current
branch do not change. In the settings of the repository on GitHub, set Pages to use the branch
`gh-pages`.

You can also build the site in a GitHub Action, and upload `_site`. smalldocs needs only one
`pip install` there.
